transcript:
Meeting: AtlasGrid — implementation orbit sync
Date: 2027-06-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 1:12:00
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Arjun (Redwood CSM), Nina (AtlasGrid Head of MLOps), Samir (AtlasGrid Platform), Evelyn (AtlasGrid Security), Rajiv (AtlasGrid SRE), Priya (AtlasGrid Product)

Summary:
Quick intake to align on network and security constraints, finalize pilot scope for Dedicated pool, schedule benchmark, and agree next steps for SOC2/KMS artifacts.

Topics:
- VPC/networking and peering
- SOC2/ISO evidence and KMS integration
- Pilot throughput targets and latency SLOs
- Onboarding timeline and runbook owners

Action items (recap at end included above)

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we've got a full house, um -- quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Nina Torres: Hi, Nina here, Head of MLOps at AtlasGrid.
[00:00:11] Samir Khatri: Samir platform eng.
[00:00:13] Evelyn Park: Evelyn, security.
[00:00:15] Rajiv Malhotra: Rajiv, SRE.
[00:00:17] Priya Desai: Priya, product.
[00:00:20] Maya Patel: Great, thanks. Liam and Arjun from our side?
[00:00:23] Liam Chen: Hey all, Liam SE. I'll be running the benchmarks and the network checks.
[00:00:26] Arjun Rao: Arjun, CSM, I'll handle onboarding cadence and runbooks.
[00:00:30] Maya Patel: Cool. Purpose today: get a clear picture of AtlasGrid's constraints so we can spin up the Dedicated pilot and run a production-like benchmark. We'll leave time for security questions near the end.
[00:00:45] Nina Torres: Sounds good. Quick context: we're migrating parts of our inference stack from an on-prem infra to a hybrid model. We need predictable latency for the search agents, and usage is roughly 8k to 12k reqs/day with occasional spikes. Our tolerance for p95 is 250 ms on request paths.
[00:01:05] Liam Chen: Got it. When you say spikes, are those concurrency spikes or long-sequence prompts?
[00:01:12] Nina Torres: Mostly concurrency -- bursts during nightly data ingest and business hours. Sequence lengths average 120 tokens with some longer conversation contexts up to 1k tokens.
[00:01:22] Samir Khatri: Also worth calling out we want to keep embeddings generation in-host for privacy, so can we talk about data residency for logs and KV cache?
[00:01:30] Maya Patel: Yes, good point. For Dedicated we can isolate logs and set retention policies; Private (VPC) option gives you full control but requires additional ops.
[00:01:40] Evelyn Park: Security first question, do you have SOC2 and ISO attestation? And how does Redwood handle customer-managed keys?
[00:01:47] Liam Chen: Short answer: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001, we can share the attestations. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration, and in Private deployments you can bring your own HSM.
[00:01:58] Evelyn Park: Okay, please send the certs. Also need details on key rotation and audit log retention.
[00:02:05] Arjun Rao: Noted. We'll attach our security pack; Maya will own delivery for certs.
[00:02:11] Maya Patel: Yep, I'll share the pack after the call.
[00:02:14] Priya Desai: For the pilot, what's the minimal config? We want something that mirrors production latencies but doesn't overcommit spend.
[00:02:22] Liam Chen: For your scale, we typically recommend a small Dedicated pool with 4x A100-equivalent instances (or Q8 quantized variants if compatible), plus autoscale headroom. That usually meets 8k-12k/day with target p95 under 200-300 ms depending on prompt mix.
[00:02:40] Samir Khatri: Clarify "A100-equivalent" — are you specifying exact GPU types? We run on GCP and prefer TPU-ish instances; compatibility matters.
[00:02:48] Liam Chen: Right, good call. We publish hardware profiles; the runtime picks kernels and quantization profiles per hardware. For GCP we'd map to the closest GPU family. We'll confirm exact SKUs for the pilot.
[00:02:58] Nina Torres: Also need to confirm how failover works if capacity is constrained — like can requests fall back to hosted variants? We need graceful degradation.
[00:03:06] Maya Patel: Yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible hosted model variant. That is configurable per route. We'll show the fallback policy in the runbook.
[00:03:15] Rajiv Malhotra: Network: we use strict egress rules. We'll need to do VPC peering or PrivateLink. What's supported?
[00:03:22] Liam Chen: Both are supported. For Dedicated, peering is typical. For Private we do VPC-only access. We'll need your allowed CIDRs and egress rules; we'll provide a template.
[00:03:31] Evelyn Park: That template should include IP ranges and ports — also TLS termination points. We can't allow plaintext traffic.
[00:03:37] Maya Patel: Understood. We'll include TLS expectations and ports.
[00:03:40] Priya Desai: Onboarding timeline — how long until we can run a meaningful benchmark? We have a product milestone mid-July.
[00:03:48] Arjun Rao: Typical Dedicated pilot onboarding is 2-3 weeks for network + provisioning and then a 1-week ramp test. We can aim for a full benchmark by the week of 2027-06-21 if network is provisioned quickly.
[00:03:59] Nina Torres: That would work. What's the acceptance criteria for the pilot?
[00:04:03] Maya Patel: Suggested acceptance: p95 latency <= 300 ms for standard request mix, throughput target of 10k reqs/day with <1% errors, and successful KMS integration for encryption-at-rest. Adjust as you prefer.
[00:04:15] Nina Torres: Let's set p95 <= 250 ms for our critical routes.
[00:04:18] Maya Patel: Noted. We'll capture that.
[00:04:21] Liam Chen: For the benchmark, we'll need sample payloads, concurrency pattern, and a spike schedule. Can you share a sanitized dataset?
[00:04:28] Priya Desai: We can provide synthetic prompts that mimic the user flows, I'll coordinate with Nina and Samir.
[00:04:33] Samir Khatri: We'll also send expected seq length distribution.
[00:04:36] Maya Patel: Great. On cost -- Dedicated committed seats have a monthly base plus token costs; we can model spend for the pilot and extrapolate. I'll send a cost model.
[00:04:46] Nina Torres: We might consider quantization to save cost; do you support int8/q8 models without significant quality drop?
[00:04:53] Liam Chen: We support multiple quantization profiles and can run a quick quality regression on a holdout prompt set. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization for your workload.
[00:05:03] Evelyn Park: One more security note — our compliance team will want to see audit logs per user and per model call. Retention of 1 year. Can Redwood provide that granularity?
[00:05:13] Liam Chen: Yes, we have token-level traces and per-request metadata; retention policies can be configured. For Dedicated and Private we can push logs to your SIEM.
[00:05:22] Rajiv Malhotra: If logs go to our SIEM, what format and throughput should we expect? We have a tight ingestion budget.
[00:05:28] Arjun Rao: We'll provide log size estimates based on expected request volume; likely small per-request JSON objects, but we'll share numbers.
[00:05:36] Nina Torres: Great. Any blockers on our side today?
[00:05:39] Samir Khatri: We need the network template and the SOC2 attestation to start internal approvals.
[00:05:43] Maya Patel: We'll send both today — I'll take ownership.
[00:05:46] Evelyn Park: Please include KMS key rotation policy and supported algorithms.
[00:05:50] Liam Chen: We'll include that in the security pack.
[00:05:52] Priya Desai: Who should we ping for day-to-day?
[00:05:55] Arjun Rao: Arjun is the CSM and primary contact for operational onboarding. Liam is technical lead. Maya is deal owner for contract and pricing.
[00:06:03] Maya Patel: Cool. Any questions from Redwood side about AtlasGrid architecture?
[00:06:07] Nina Torres: One more: we use an internal feature flag for model rollout. Can Redwood integrate with our rollout pipeline so we can canary across 10% users?
[00:06:16] Liam Chen: We have rollout policies (canary/A-B) at route-level; we can integrate with your flags via a webhook or by setting percentage-based routing. We'll draft an example.
[00:06:25] Nina Torres: Perfect.
[00:06:27] Priya Desai: Timeline recap?
[00:06:29] Arjun Rao: Action items: network template + SOC2 pack (Maya) by 2027-06-04, onboarding runbook (Arjun) by 2027-06-06, benchmark plan (Liam) by 2027-06-08, pricing and SOW (Maya) by 2027-06-07. Aim to run benchmark third week of June.
[00:06:45] Maya Patel: Sounds good.
[00:06:47] Evelyn Park: Quick note — our procurement expects a standard DPA and security addendum, any templates we can preview?
[00:06:54] Maya Patel: Yes, I'll drop the DPA and SAA in the doc bundle.
[00:06:58] Nina Torres: Thanks everyone.
[00:07:00] Samir Khatri: Thanks.
[00:07:02] Rajiv Malhotra: Cheers.
[00:07:05] Liam Chen: One last technical detail — we'll need to confirm your average token payload size; I'll send a small parser script to help you compute it from logs.
[00:07:13] Priya Desai: We'll get that to you.
[00:07:16] Arjun Rao: Ok final recap in the notes, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window.
[00:07:22] Maya Patel: Thanks all, call adjourned.

(End of recording)
